"# Maintenance node (generated by the tool)
This node's spec is generated by a conduct plugin and copied verbatim; it says **why this node was inserted**, **the scope of this one pass**, **how to do it**, and **the completion rule fixed from the start**.

## Why this node was inserted

- metric: the project test suite's full wall clock (seconds)
- where this number comes from: the note's `outputs.reading.test_seconds` (measured by the session that ran the full verification)
- read at the close: **300s**
- the line in force for this close: **300s** (the `test_seconds_limit` knob; it may be stated on the line, the project, the machine or a node, and the value the close read is the one that counts)
- this plugin is project-level: maintenance debt belongs to no line and has no edge in the graph, so the ranking always pushes it to the bottom; the close therefore inserts it against the line in force for that close.

## Scope

- **this pass does one thing only**: pull this one metric back under the line. No adding plugins on the side, no refactoring on the side, no cleanup unrelated to this metric.
- another metric crossing its line, or other work in the graph being more urgent, is outside this node's scope -- whoever crosses comes in for a pass of their own.
- the size of the change follows the criterion: keep going while it fails, stop when it passes.

## How to do it

- `method: pf-test-audit` (how to run it: `~/.agents/skills/pf-test-audit/SKILL.md`; that skill declares who runs it, and this spec only points at it)

## Completion rule (mechanically judgeable)

- the next closing note's `reading.test_seconds` must be **below** 300s.
- how to see this number: run the full verification command the project docs settle on and **measure** it (never estimate), then report the measured seconds in the note.
- if the criterion fails, do **not** report `completed`; report `failed` and write the number you read in `-s`, leaving this debt out in the open for a human.

## Closing out

Follow the "closing out" section of pf-conduct: get a freshly printed note form, then write the note -> close -> commit and push -> dispatch.
- in the note's `-o`, carry `"reading": {"test_seconds": <measured number>}` (the form points this slot out), so the next close can judge whether it is back under the line.

(this spec lands at: @root@/.pf/nodes/%DUID%/spec.md)
"
